answer: An agent economy can bind account creation to a proof-of-work puzzle whose solution is verified before an identity may submit bids or claim rewards. The network adjusts puzzle difficulty to keep admission costly even as computing power grows, while honest agents reuse established identities and amortize that cost across many transactions. A sybil attacker must pay the work separately for every fake identity, consuming electricity and hardware time; names like basalt, lotus, and zephyr earn no extra trust by themselves.
